doc.title: Roscoe Mitchell interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, May 23, 2023

chapter: Performing and the idea of free jazz
title: Not tempted by soul jazz or fusion; early music and Baroque flute
summary: He follows only what he wants to do and studies all kinds of music, including the Baroque flute and recorders.

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone
story.community_name: Reeds, mouthpieces and horns: the reed player's gear

blocks.x: In your career as time went by and you saw other jazz musicians seemingly selling a lot of records and we think that makes money for them, that may or may not be true. But did you ever look at that and say — be tempted to go that route? Soul jazz or fusion?

No I ain’t tempted by nothing but what I want to do. You know there’s something that guides me you know. You know like I said, a good day for me is when I can wake up and learn something you know. And music is like hey I need more than one lifetime to learn as much about music as I would like to know. So I give in to that. I give in to that you know. I mean and I’m studying all kinds of music you know. Early music you know. I play the transverso — the flute with six holes and one key that’s down at the bottom. This is the instrument that Bach wrote for you know.
The Baroque flute you’re talking about.
